claims.text: Local variations in lattice distortion and short-range chemical order determine the effective electron-phonon coupling strength in high-entropy superconducting alloys.
Effective electron-phonon coupling strength controls the superconducting transition temperature Tc.
(TaNb)1-x(HfZrTi)x-type solid solutions can be superconducting.
The proposed initial alloy is nearly equiatomic.
The initial alloy is fully chemically disordered.
The relevant initial state is an as-cast alloy.
The initial alloy exhibits superconductivity in the dirty limit.
Controlled thermal annealing reduces local lattice distortions while preserving overall composition.
Controlled thermal annealing increases short-range chemical order.
Local lattice distortion and short-range chemical order modulate the local electron-phonon interaction environment.
Reducing distortion and enhancing short-range order strengthens local electron-phonon coupling.
Annealing-induced structural improvement reduces impurity scattering.
Stronger electron-phonon coupling and reduced disorder-related scattering lead to an increased Tc.
Annealing that enhances short-range order will produce a narrower superconducting transition than the as-cast baseline.
The as-cast, fully disordered baseline has a lower Tc and broader superconducting transition than the proposed annealed state.
The mechanism applies under moderate annealing that changes local order without causing long-range crystallization or phase separation.
Heat-capacity and upper-critical-field analyses support conventional BCS-like pairing with intermediate-to-strong coupling in superconducting HEAs.
Isotope studies provide prior evidence for phonon mediation in these alloys.
The contribution of enhanced electron-phonon coupling relative to disorder-induced scattering is quantitatively uncertain.
Failure to observe either a statistically significant Tc increase or a correlation between enhanced short-range order and stronger electron-phonon signatures would falsify the hypothesis.
